mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) consistently predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as elevated joblessness signals economic weakness that depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of observations when UNRATE is above its 10-year median, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days through improved corporate revenue outlooks.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS rise above their 3-month moving averages, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), persistent price pressures prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as higher rates suppress equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of high-inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 120.0, it indicates strong manufacturing activity and economic growth, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days through immediate earnings momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO > 120.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) consistently predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days, as increased residential construction activity reflects broad economic strength and rising consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of observations when HOUST is above its 5-year median, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) combined with a stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals that the Fed is delaying policy tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as investors anticipate sustained liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS remains stable, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an impending slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of late-cycle expansion periods when UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC over 2-year windows is below 0.03.
